_about: Clinic heal game `foot` (D15i, decision 27; js/clinic/heal/games/foot.js). The sole of the foot, toes up. The soak (which water: paani [hot]/[cold]/[lukewarm], how many jugs), then each splinter dragged out along its lighter channel with square turns to the edge of the foot: touching the side is an 'ow', it slides back to the last turn and loses the steady-hand row (a scored skill row, no words); then a plaster on each spot. Level 1 one straight channel; level 2 two channels with one or two turns; level 3 three channels from three toes, three turns each and narrower, the toes named for the order (pela [big toe], ne poi ...). Sides only in the diagnosis (D10). The channels, splinters and widths are in the code (PATHS, halfW per level); the levels, rows and words below the game's code are the older design's notes, kept for reference.

sore-feet.english: sore feet from dancing all night at the wedding (and a thorn from the garden)

paani.english: paani (the jug: hot or cold is chosen in the game)

loon.english: loon (the salt pot and its spoon)

foot-why._src: moved out of the game's code into its data so the engine holds it (step 4e, G26); English placeholder, to record

foot-goal._src: moved out of the game's code into its data so the engine holds it (step 4e, G26); English placeholder, to record

1._note: The bath (hot or cold paani) + two toe calls by size (either foot) + the thorn in the sore foot (it shows a swirl), named by size + the plaster. Lines one at a time.

2._note: + the salt count (hakro/ba/trae chamcho loon); three toe calls. Said as one list.

3._note: + the side, in the patient's voice, on every toe (size x side: one toe of ten); no swirl shows which foot.

camera._about: D2 (1 Oct): the sole is seen from the front-on wide shot (the art plan §2.1).
camera._target: A1 (5 Oct): the match cut. target = where the close-up draws the sore part and size = its radius, in the close-up's 800 x 500 units: the push-in ends with the patient's part (from the art's anchor) at that place and size.

art._about: The art plan's P1 (closeups/<set>/sole.webp, child and adult sets), swapped in by file name when it exists; the channels and splinters stay code.

place._about: A1 (5 Oct): P1 placed so its big toe (360, 195 in the 1024 x 1536 source) and little toe (750, 397) land on the mirrored stand-in's (298, 70) and (508, 78): the sole's width and length match the stand-in's outline, so the channels and their clip still fit. The art's toes slope down to the little toe where the stand-in's are level, so the levels with channels from the toes, toes named (level 2 and up since Zafar's heal ladder, 13 Oct) keep the stand-in until the toes are re-placed. Mirrored in code when the big toe is on the right.
place._s07: s07-clinic-a (RP1, CLN-87's foot note): the sole redone with level toes (sole-v2, cut by artcut.py s07.cut.json): its big toe centre (355, 229 in the 1024 x 1536 source) on the mirrored stand-in's (298, 70) and its little toe (760, 289) on (508, 78) at one scale (0.5185): every toe sits in its stand-in channel, so levels 1-3 draw it (the v1 box is box_v1)

art._s08b: s08-w5b (CLN-192; Zafar 18 Oct: 'the foot kind of floats ... the ankle ... just stops dead ... blow it out into the background'): the s08b FT1 sole, its leg running on off the bottom edge (no cuff), registered on sole-v3 / sole-v2 (artcut shift -0.9 px), so place.box is unchanged

channel._about: s08-w5b (CLN-193; Zafar 18 Oct: 'an irritated raised red translucent channel and you see the splinter traveling inside of it'; 'a repeatable, very tileable visual block ... and the splinter as well'): the s08b SP1 pieces, laid along each path by js/clinic/heal/games/foot.js layChannel. straightBand = the straight block's [first, last opaque row, first, last opaque col, w, h] (px), repeated along each segment; cornerBox = the elbow's [centre x, centre y, arm width, w, h] (arms up and right), turned onto each turn; endBox = the closed end's [cap centre x, centre y, band width, w, h] (the cap at its right), at the splinter's spot; opacity = how see-through the welt is over the splinter (CLN-193); splinterAspect = the splinter's length over its thickness; welt = the share of the channel's width the pieces show through (a soft mask along the path: their own skin-coloured flanks and square ends stay hidden), feather its soft edge (shares of the width)
